newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rebound on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rebound on foreign buying.

text.p: Israeli shares recovered from early losses on Thursday to close mixed thanks to aggressive buying by foreign investors, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares fell 0.38 percent, or 1.02 points, to 266.53 on all-share turnover of 160 million shekels against 207 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.07 percent higher at 274.43.

"The session opened with a mild decline and by midday the indices fell by 1.3 percent. Just before the end of the trading day foreign investors started buying Maof shares aggressively and the whole market recovered," said a trader at Evergreen Capital Markets.

"The correction that started on Wednesday continued today. Towards the end of the day foreign investors increased their activity in specific shares that are identified with them," said Ronen Kaufman of Nesuah Trading and Investments.

Supersol, the main gainer on the Maof, rose 3.0 percent to 1,070 agorot recovering from an early decline of one percent. Traders said Supersol is one of the stocks most favoured by overseas investors.
"Foreign investors tend to focus on the large cap stocks. If it wasn't for them the whole market would have closed lower," Kaufman added.

"Many investors wait for a correction to start buying so the market has difficulties going through a real consolidation," the Evergreen trader said. "The small capitalisation stocks were today's main losers because they couldn't react on time to the market's recovery."

The most active shares were Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 1.5 percent to 20,020 agorot on volume of 10.5 million shekels; Koor Industries, which fell 0.5 percent to 34,843 agorot on turnover of 7.8 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which gained 2.5 percent to 417 on volume of 7.0 million shekels.

Africa Israel Investments plunged 8.5 percent to 24,654 agorot on very low turnover of only 479,000 shekels. "This was only an accident. I am sure that the share will recover on Sunday," Kaufman said.
